interface.name: zwlr_layer_shell_v1

description.summary: create surfaces that are layers of the desktop

interface.description: Clients can use this interface to assign the layer_surface role to wl_surfaces. Such surfaces are assigned to a "layer" of the output and rendered with a defined z-depth respective to each other. They may also be anchored to the edges and corners of a screen and specify input handling semantics. This interface should be suitable for the implementation of many desktop shell components, and a broad number of other features that overlay or place windows with respect to the desktop.

request.name: get_layer_surface

description.summary: create a layer_surface from a surface

request.description:
Create a layer surface for an existing surface. This assigns the role of layer_surface, or raises a protocol error if another role is already assigned.
Creating a layer surface from a wl_surface which has a buffer attached or committed is a client error, and any attempts by a client to attach or manipulate a buffer prior to the first layer_surface.configure call must also be treated as errors.
You may pass NULL for output to allow the compositor to decide which output to use. Generally this will be the one that the user most recently interacted with.
The provided surface must be visible as a top-level surface when the role is assigned. Layer surfaces are not visible as toplevel surfaces, so if the wl_surface is not a toplevel surface, it will be treated as a client error.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will not use the layer shell object any more. Objects that have been created through this instance are not affected.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: wl_surface has a buffer attached or committed

enum.name: layer
enum.description: These values indicate which layers a surface can be rendered in. They are ordered by z depth, bottom-most first. Traditional shell surfaces will typically be rendered between the bottom and top layers. Fullscreen shell surfaces are typically rendered at the top layer. Popups and other user interface elements are typically at overlay. But this is not guaranteed.

interface.name: zwlr_layer_surface_v1
interface.description:
An interface that may be implemented by a wl_surface, for surfaces that describe a layer surface.
This interface exposes requests and events relevant for describing and positioning a layer surface.

request.name: set_size

description.summary: sets the size of the surface

request.description:
Sets the size of the surface in surface-local coordinates. The compositor will display the surface centered with respect to the anchors.
If you pass 0 for either value, the compositor will assign it and inform you of the assignment in the configure event. You must set your anchor to opposite edges in the dimensions you omit; not doing so is a protocol error. Both values are 0 by default.

request.name: set_anchor

description.summary: configures the anchor point of the surface

request.description:
Requests that the compositor anchor the surface to the specified edges and corners. If two orthogonal edges are specified (e.g. 'top' and 'left'), then the anchor point will be the intersection of the edges (e.g. the top left corner of the output); if only one edge is specified, then the anchor point will be centered on that edge.
A single edge or corner can be specified, but not both. Setting an anchor point that does not touch any edge is a protocol error. Setting two edges on the same axis is a protocol error.

request.name: set_exclusive_zone

description.summary: configures the exclusive geometry of this surface

request.description:
Requests that the compositor avoids occluding an area of the surface with other surfaces. This is primarily intended for surfaces using the top or bottom layer, to reserve screen space. The compositor's usage of this space is dependent on the value of set_anchor.
A positive value sets the size of the exclusive zone to the given value in surface-local coordinates. A value of 0 requests the compositor to not reserve any space. A value of -1 requests the compositor to not occlude the surface with other surfaces.

request.name: set_margin

description.summary: sets a margin from the anchor point

request.description: Requests that the surface be placed some distance away from the anchor point, in surface-local coordinates.

request.name: set_keyboard_interactivity
request.description:
Set how keyboard events are requested for this surface.
The keyboard_interactivity value can be one of the following:
none: no keyboard events are requested. The compositor is free to not forward keyboard events to the layer surface.
exclusive: exclusive keyboard focus. This asks the compositor to give all keyboard events to this surface and not pass them on to any other surface in the same seat.
on_demand: regular keyboard focus. The compositor will forward keyboard events to the surface when it has keyboard focus.

request.name: get_popup

description.summary: assign this layer_surface as an xdg_popup parent

request.description: This assigns an xdg_popup's parent to this layer_surface. This popup should have been created via xdg_surface::get_popup with the parent set to NULL, and this request must be invoked before committing the popup's surface state.

request.name: ack_configure
request.description:
When a configure event is received, if a client commits the surface in response to the configure event, the client must make an ack_configure request sometime before the commit request, passing along the serial of the configure event.
For instance, for configure events the compositor can use the serial to let the client know which configure event its acking.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request informs the compositor that the layer surface is to be destroyed. The compositor is expected to hide the surface and then send the wl_surface.unmap event.

event.name: configure
event.description:
The configure event asks the client to resize its surface.
Clients should arrange their surface for the new states, and then send an ack_configure request with the serial sent in this configure event at some point before committing the new surface.

event.name: closed
event.description: The closed event is sent by the compositor when it wants the surface to be closed. The client should then destroy the surface.
